+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib
+
+matplotlib.use("Agg")
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+source = (ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet").as_posix()
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+annual = con.execute(
+    f"""
+    SELECT
+      year(crash_date) AS year,
+      count(*) AS all_crashes,
+      count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough IS NULL) AS null_borough_crashes,
+      count(*) FILTER (WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN') AS brooklyn_crashes,
+      sum(number_of_pedestrians_injured) FILTER (WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN') AS pedestrians_injured,
+      sum(number_of_pedestrians_killed) FILTER (WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN') AS pedestrians_killed,
+      count(*) FILTER (
+        WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN'
+          AND (number_of_pedestrians_injured > 0 OR number_of_pedestrians_killed > 0)
+      ) AS pedestrian_harm_crashes,
+      count(*) FILTER (
+        WHERE borough = 'BROOKLYN'
+          AND (number_of_pedestrians_injured IS NULL OR number_of_pedestrians_killed IS NULL)
+      ) AS brooklyn_null_pedestrian_counts
+    FROM read_parquet('{source}')
+    WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
+    GROUP BY 1
+    ORDER BY 1
+    """
+).df()
+annual["null_borough_share_pct"] = 100 * annual.null_borough_crashes / annual.all_crashes
+annual["pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000"] = (
+    1000 * annual.pedestrian_harm_crashes / annual.brooklyn_crashes
+)
+
+# Both endpoint years are fully represented; 2012 and 2026 are partial and not plotted.
+coverage = con.execute(
+    f"""
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year, min(crash_date) AS first_date, max(crash_date) AS last_date
+    FROM read_parquet('{source}')
+    WHERE year(crash_date) IN (2012, 2013, 2025, 2026)
+    GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
+    """
+).df()
+print("Coverage:")
+print(coverage.to_string(index=False))
+print("Annual null-borough shares (%):")
+print(annual[["year", "null_borough_share_pct"]].to_string(index=False))
+assert annual.year.tolist() == list(range(2013, 2026))
+assert annual.brooklyn_null_pedestrian_counts.sum() == 0
+
+years = annual.year.astype(int)
+null_share_by_year = ", ".join(
+    f"{int(row.year)}: {row.null_borough_share_pct:.1f}%"
+    for row in annual.itertuples()
+)
+exclusion_sentence = (
+    f"Rows with NULL borough are excluded; their share of all rows in each plotted year was "
+    f"{null_share_by_year}. No Brooklyn rows have NULL pedestrian injury or death counts. "
+    "The partial 2012 (July–December) and 2026 (January 1–June 11) years are excluded."
+)
+
+def save_line(values, y, ylabel, title, filename, color, integer=True):
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10.5, 5.8), constrained_layout=True)
+    ax.plot(values.year, values[y], color=color, linewidth=2.8, marker="o", markersize=5.5)
+    ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=16, weight="bold", pad=16)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
+    ax.set_xticks(values.year)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", color="#d8dee6", linewidth=0.8)
+    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+    ax.spines[["left", "bottom"]].set_color("#aab4c0")
+    if integer:
+        ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(plt.MaxNLocator(integer=True))
+    for x, value in zip(values.year, values[y]):
+        ax.annotate(f"{int(value):,}" if integer else f"{value:.1f}", (x, value),
+                    xytext=(0, 8), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=8)
+    fig.text(0.01, 0.005,
+             "Source: NYC police-reported motor vehicle crashes; Brooklyn borough field. Full years 2013–2025.",
+             fontsize=8, color="#4b5563")
+    fig.savefig(OUT / filename, dpi=180, facecolor="white")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+injury_values = annual[["year", "pedestrians_injured"]].copy()
+injury_values.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+save_line(injury_values, "pedestrians_injured", "Pedestrians injured (people)",
+          "Brooklyn pedestrian injuries fell from 2013, then climbed", "option_1.png", "#176b87")
+
+fatality_values = annual[["year", "pedestrians_killed"]].copy()
+fatality_values.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+save_line(fatality_values, "pedestrians_killed", "Pedestrians killed (people)",
+          "Brooklyn pedestrian deaths: annual counts fluctuate", "option_2.png", "#b33d3d")
+
+rate_values = annual[["year", "pedestrian_harm_crashes", "brooklyn_crashes",
+                      "pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000"]].copy()
+rate_values["pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000"] = rate_values[
+    "pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000"
+].round(2)
+rate_values.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False)
+save_line(rate_values, "pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000",
+          "Crashes with pedestrian injury or death per 1,000 Brooklyn crashes",
+          "Pedestrian-harm crashes became more common per reported Brooklyn crash",
+          "option_3.png", "#6953a3", integer=False)
+
+first, last = annual.iloc[0], annual.iloc[-1]
+inj_pct = (last.pedestrians_injured / first.pedestrians_injured - 1) * 100
+death_pct = (last.pedestrians_killed / first.pedestrians_killed - 1) * 100
+rate_pct = (last.pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000 /
+            first.pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000 - 1) * 100
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians injured in police-reported Brooklyn crashes",
+            "denominator": "None (annual count)",
+            "grouping": "Crash year",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "Injury counts directly measure the reported nonfatal pedestrian harm and provide a clear year-by-year trend.",
+            "probability": 0.4,
+            "answer": (f"Reported Brooklyn pedestrian injuries declined from {int(first.pedestrians_injured):,} in 2013 "
+                       f"to {int(last.pedestrians_injured):,} in 2025 ({abs(inj_pct):.1f}% lower), though they rose "
+                       f"from a low of {int(annual.pedestrians_injured.min()):,} in 2020."),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers whether the annual number of pedestrians injured has improved: the chart shows a long decline from 2013 through 2020, followed by a substantial rebound through 2025. "
+                "Annual injury counts are a direct measure of reported nonfatal harm, although they are not a per-walking-trip risk measure. "
+                "It leaves fatal harm and the likelihood of injury per pedestrian trip unanswered, and cannot establish why the trend changed. "
+                + exclusion_sentence
+            ),
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed in police-reported Brooklyn crashes",
+            "denominator": "None (annual count)",
+            "grouping": "Crash year",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "Fatalities are the most severe outcome and can move differently from nonfatal injuries.",
+            "probability": 0.25,
+            "answer": (f"Reported Brooklyn pedestrian deaths rose from {int(first.pedestrians_killed)} in 2013 to "
+                       f"{int(last.pedestrians_killed)} in 2025 ({death_pct:.1f}% higher), with sizable year-to-year fluctuations."),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers whether the most severe reported pedestrian outcome improved: the chart shows volatile annual deaths and more deaths in 2025 than in 2013. "
+                "Fatality counts matter independently because a decline in nonfatal injuries would not imply fewer deaths. "
+                "It leaves nonfatal injury burden and fatality risk per walking trip unanswered, and small annual counts make the trend uneven. "
+                + exclusion_sentence
+            ),
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Brooklyn crash rows with at least one pedestrian injured or killed per 1,000 Brooklyn crash rows",
+            "denominator": "All Brooklyn police-reported crash rows in the same year",
+            "grouping": "Crash year",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "The per-crash share accounts for changes in the volume of Brooklyn crash reports while measuring how often reported crashes involve pedestrian harm.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": (f"Pedestrian-harm crashes increased from {first.pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000:.1f} per 1,000 Brooklyn crash rows in 2013 "
+                       f"to {last.pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000:.1f} in 2025 ({rate_pct:.1f}% higher), despite fewer total Brooklyn crash rows."),
+            "interpretation": (
+                "This framing answers how frequently police-reported Brooklyn crashes involved at least one pedestrian injury or death: the rate per 1,000 crash rows fell to 2020 and then rose above its 2013 level by 2025. "
+                "Its denominator adjusts for variation in the number of reported Brooklyn crashes, making it a defensible crash-level comparison. "
+                "It leaves pedestrian exposure and risk per walking trip unanswered, and is not a population- or traffic-adjusted safety rate. "
+                + exclusion_sentence
+            ),
+        },
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+
+# Print the exact endpoint values and percentage changes used in the answers for review.
+print("Endpoint comparisons:")
+print(json.dumps({
+    "injuries_2013": int(first.pedestrians_injured), "injuries_2025": int(last.pedestrians_injured),
+    "injury_change_pct": round(inj_pct, 1),
+    "deaths_2013": int(first.pedestrians_killed), "deaths_2025": int(last.pedestrians_killed),
+    "death_change_pct": round(death_pct, 1),
+    "harm_crashes_per_1000_2013": round(first.pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000, 1),
+    "harm_crashes_per_1000_2025": round(last.pedestrian_harm_crashes_per_1000, 1),
+    "rate_change_pct": round(rate_pct, 1),
+    "brooklyn_crashes_2013": int(first.brooklyn_crashes), "brooklyn_crashes_2025": int(last.brooklyn_crashes),
+}, indent=2))
